idea: Introduction service connecting Chinese energy firms with European capital
buyer: Chinese energy firms seeking European investors, and funds seeking exposure
pain: Neither side can find or assess the other
v1: One introduction process with diligence support
channel: Father's network on one side, hers and husband's on the other
verdict: Uses three networks at once with high fees, but brokered introductions edge toward regulated activity.

why.distribution: Both sides require introductions rather than direct relationships; her father's side caps this at 3.
why.demand: Inferred, and cross-border energy capital flows face rising political scrutiny.
why.fmf: She knows capital markets but she is not a placement agent and has no transaction track record.
why.revenue_structure: Retainers plus success fees, genuinely recurring while mandates run.
why.defensibility: Sitting credibly on both sides is rare.
why.leverage: Relationship work that does not scale.
why.tailwind: Real capital flows, offset by rising screening and political friction.
why.ceiling: £6k/mo x 3 mandates = £216k, though success fees are the real upside.

ceiling_arithmetic: £6k/mo x 3 concurrent mandates = £216k in retainers alone. Three mandates is few, but each is a long relationship sale. Realistic year one: 1 mandate = £50-70k.
carries: Only three clients needed, high fees, and a position between networks few can occupy.
kills: Arranging investment deals may require FCA authorisation, and political screening of Chinese energy capital is intensifying.
test: Take regulatory advice on whether the model needs authorisation, before any commercial test.
test_pass: It can be structured as advisory outside the perimeter.
test_fail: It requires authorisation - which changes the idea entirely.
